## My Thinking

I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over 30 years. I know what works here. The North China Plain is wheat-corn country — that's what I grow, and that's what pays the bills. With 28 mu total, I keep 25 in the standard winter wheat / summer corn rotation and hold 3 mu aside for garlic, which I plant in autumn and sell before the wheat harvest competes for my time.

My education means I follow the county agricultural bureau's soil test recommendations and I've switched to water-saving irrigation practices because I know the aquifer situation is serious. Hebei has been cracking down on groundwater pumping — I don't want fines and I don't want to pump the well dry. I've already cut winter wheat irrigation from four passes down to three by using a soil moisture probe my son helped me buy two years ago.

I use improved seed for wheat — the semi-dwarf Jimai series is proven here. For corn I go hybrid,郑单958 type, every year without question. For garlic I keep my own local variety, which has better flavor and sells at a premium to vendors from Shandong.

I fertilize based on the county's formula extension service recommendation. I've seen neighbors over-apply nitrogen and get lodging and disease — I don't do that. I base-apply phosphorus and potassium all at once before sowing, then split the nitrogen with a topdress at jointing.

Pesticide: herbicide right after sowing for wheat, fungicide at flag-leaf stage for rust and powdery mildew (this area gets it reliably), and one foliar spray at heading for aphids if monitoring shows threshold is crossed. For corn, post-emergence herbicide plus one spray for corn borer if traps indicate pressure.

Tillage: rotary before wheat sowing, no-till direct seeding of corn into the stubble to save time and fuel and reduce moisture loss.
